routes.description: Establish that consciousness or mind is fundamental by presenting idealism as the more economical explanation of experience, information, causation, and observer-linked quantum phenomena, while supplying an account of physical development and an empirical condition that could undermine the view.
routes.successCriteria: The route succeeds if its ontology explains experienced and physical regularities without an indispensable material substrate, connects quantum observation to consciousness without preventing pre-observer development, and identifies a publicly examinable way in which the account could fail.

motionBridge.description: Show that idealism and the cited quantum considerations jointly provide good reason to treat consciousness or a divine mind as fundamental.

centralBridges.description: Establish a cumulative inference from mental correlations, top-down causation, informational structure, and limits of material reduction to an idealist ontology.
Explain how informational evolution and observer-linked definite appearances can accommodate physical interaction and cosmic development before local conscious observers.
State empirical implications or potential defeaters that make the consciousness-dependent account publicly examinable rather than insulated from evidence.

subsidiaryBridges.description: Support the ontology by arguing that experienced properties and informational distinctions do not require an additional material substance.
Clarify what interactions and structures remain as informational evolution when no thinking observer produces definite spatiotemporal appearances.

routes.description: Require independently confirmable manifestations and mind-independent causal interaction for the affirmative claim, distinguish legitimate inference from unsupported ontology, and test whether consciousness-dependent physics explains preconscious development or instead adds an unfalsifiable divine or mental condition.
routes.successCriteria: The route succeeds if the proposed idealist and quantum inferences lack independently demonstrable support, fail to account for physical interaction and development without observer dependence, or do not yield discriminating empirical consequences sufficient to justify fundamentality.

motionBridge.description: Show that the claim of fundamental consciousness or divine mind fails the relevant public-demonstrability or physical-interaction requirements.

centralBridges.description: Establish that burden-bearing claims require detectable, repeatable, and independently confirmable consequences in shared reality.
Distinguish inferences built from mutually reinforcing demonstrable evidence from an idealist inference whose components may not independently support its ontology.
Account for forces, chemistry, and physical development through causal relations that do not depend on being mentally experienced.
Determine whether observer-dependent reality has a discriminating falsification condition and whether its additional mental commitments perform necessary explanatory work.

subsidiaryBridges.description: Test the account against evolution and chemical interaction occurring before ordinary conscious observers were present.
Examine whether informational and video-game analogies entail the claimed absence of definite or maintained unobserved physical structure.

sections.title: Public Evidence and Explanatory Inference
sections.rationale: This issue sets the governing evidential burden and tests whether the affirmative cumulative inference resembles established evidence-based inference closely enough to support a fundamental ontology.

sections.title: Information, Experience, and Material Substrate
sections.rationale: This issue addresses whether experienced properties, mathematics, and informational distinctions make matter explanatorily redundant or whether physical properties denote mind-independent causal capacities.

sections.title: Observer Dependence and Preconscious Development
sections.rationale: This issue is central to whether an observer-linked quantum account can accommodate evolution, chemistry, and continuing interaction before local minds without relying on an unexplained divine observer.

sections.title: Unobserved Reality and Physical Interaction
sections.rationale: This issue tests what persists without thinking minds and whether analogies involving rendering or informational evolution support the claimed relation between observation, spacetime definiteness, and causal interaction.

sections.title: Falsifiability and Ontological Parsimony
sections.rationale: This issue determines whether the consciousness-dependent account exposes itself to a discriminating empirical defeater and whether its ontological commitments satisfy the debate's demonstrability and economy requirements.

moves.speaker: Matt Dillahunty
moves.proposition: A publicly demonstrable claim must yield detectable interactions with shared reality that different observers can independently examine, confirm, and repeat.
moves.attributionBasis: The exchange directly identifies Matt as defining his own standard of demonstrability in response to the preceding question.

response.rationale: This constructive move establishes the con side's governing evidential standard and therefore has no earlier opposing target to answer.

responsivenessWithinClass.rationale: Within constructive moves, it clearly states a usable and central standard of public demonstrability.

precisionFindings.rationale: The shared-reality assumption, independent confirmation requirement, and sensory-exploratory basis are all expressly recoverable.

calibrationFindings.rationale: The necessity claim is appropriately framed as Matt's stated standard after explicitly setting aside hard solipsism.

logicalCoherence.rationale: Given the expressly shared universe, independent sensory confirmation coherently supplies a public-demonstrability criterion, though repeatability is compressed.

evidenceWarrant.rationale: The standard is grounded in shared observation and independent confirmation, with only a bounded defense of why these conditions are exhaustive.

relevanceBurden.rationale: Within the central tier, this directly establishes the indispensable public-evidence standard for the con route.

representationalCharity.rationale: The move defines an evidential standard rather than interpreting a meaningful live opposing alternative.

moves.evidenceBasis: Matt expressly brackets hard solipsism, assumes a shared universe, and requires independent examination and confirmation by others.

moves.speaker: Michael Jones
moves.proposition: Idealism is presented as an inference to the best explanation supported cumulatively by mental correlations, claimed top-down causation, quantum-cognition evidence, and the asserted failure to reduce consciousness to matter.
moves.attributionBasis: Michael explicitly compares his inferential case with acceptance of evolution and then enumerates the data he regards as supporting idealism.

components.text: Show independently examinable, confirmable, and repeatable interactions with shared reality.

response.rationale: The cumulative inference is issue-bearing contrary material, but enumerating correlations and alleged causation does not establish their independent confirmability or repeatability.

responsivenessWithinClass.rationale: Within relevant nonanswers, it supplies a competing inferential framework but leaves the decisive public-confirmation demand uncontacted.

precisionFindings.rationale: The cumulative inference is recoverable, but 'data,' 'quantum cognition,' and 'top-down causation' remain materially underspecified.

calibrationFindings.rationale: Claims of strong evidence and absent reduction outrun the compressed presentation and do not acknowledge substantial rival explanations.

charity.alternative: The public standard permits cumulative inference when its component evidence is independently demonstrable.
charity.decisiveQualification: The listed components still require independent support and an explicit bridge from correlations to idealism.

logicalCoherence.rationale: A cumulative inference can be valid, but the span leaves a substantial bridge from heterogeneous correlations and nonreduction to idealism.

evidenceWarrant.rationale: The conclusion relies on asserted evidence categories without representative findings, defended independence, or comparison against serious materialist rivals.

relevanceBurden.rationale: Within the central tier, the move directly advances the affirmative's principal cumulative explanatory inference.

representationalCharity.rationale: The evolution comparison recognizes inference as legitimate but omits the decisive qualification concerning demonstrable components and rival ontology.

moves.evidenceBasis: Michael compares his case to evolutionary inference and lists mental correlations, quantum cognition, top-down causation, and failed material reduction.

moves.speaker: Matt Dillahunty
moves.proposition: Evolutionary inference is supported by independently demonstrable and mutually reinforcing components, including overlapping dating methods and statistical treatment of anomalies.
moves.attributionBasis: The turn begins with a direct exception to Michael's analogy and develops Matt's contrasting account of evidential support for evolution.

components.text: Establish that the listed considerations jointly support idealism as the best explanation.

response.rationale: Matt identifies the missing property in the analogy: evolutionary inference is assembled from independently demonstrable, mutually checking components, unlike the merely listed idealist considerations.

responsivenessWithinClass.rationale: Within diagnostic defeats, it expressly identifies the defective analogy and states the evidential consequence for the cumulative inference.

precisionFindings.rationale: The contrast between inference generally and inference from independently demonstrable components is explicit and consistently maintained.

calibrationFindings.rationale: The move makes a bounded comparative evidential claim rather than claiming that inference itself guarantees truth.

charity.alternative: Idealism may also rest on a cumulative body of mutually reinforcing evidence rather than direct proof.
charity.decisiveQualification: Its individual components must still be shown independently demonstrable and mutually supportive of the ontology.

logicalCoherence.rationale: The distinction between inference and the evidential quality of its premises directly resolves the strongest validity challenge to the comparison.

evidenceWarrant.rationale: Radiometric dating and overlapping methods are representative support, though the span only compresses their independence and anomaly treatment.

relevanceBurden.rationale: Within the central tier, the move directly supplies the con route's indispensable comparison between evidential inferences.

representationalCharity.rationale: Matt grants that science uses inference and accurately locates the dispute in the demonstrability and reinforcement of its components.

moves.evidenceBasis: Matt grants that science is inferential, then contrasts sturdy demonstrable components and overlapping dating methods with Michael's listed considerations.

moves.speaker: Michael Jones
moves.proposition: Because an object can be described through felt and perceived properties, Occam's razor is said to favor mental phenomena or mental information over positing an additional material substance beneath those properties.
moves.attributionBasis: Michael marks the argument as one of his main arguments and develops it through mental properties, simulation analogy, and Hume's bundle theory.

components.text: Show that the idealist inference is built from independently demonstrable and mutually reinforcing components.
Supply consequences that different observers can independently examine, confirm, and repeat.

response.rationale: The bundle and parsimony argument advances a different affirmative consideration but does not answer either demand for independent demonstrability or sturdy inferential components.

responsivenessWithinClass.rationale: Within relevant nonanswers, it bears on ontology and economy but does not contact either decisive evidential demand.

precisionFindings.rationale: The parsimony claim is recoverable, but 'mental properties,' 'mental information,' and 'substance' are not sharply distinguished.

calibrationFindings.rationale: Describability through experienced qualities is treated as favoring mental ontology without qualifying the gap between description and causal constitution.

charity.alternative: Physical substance may explain causal capacities even if objects are experienced only through perceived qualities.
charity.decisiveQualification: Experiential access alone does not show that a physical substrate is explanatorily idle.

logicalCoherence.rationale: The inference substantially equivocates between describing an object through experience and establishing that its underlying constitution is mental.

evidenceWarrant.rationale: The simulation and bundle considerations illustrate the proposal but provide little support that material causal structure is redundant.

relevanceBurden.rationale: Within the subsidiary tier, the move directly and strongly advances the affirmative parsimony bridge.

representationalCharity.rationale: The argument treats the substrate chiefly as an extra posit and omits its strongest proposed role in grounding causal interaction.

moves.evidenceBasis: Michael describes paper through felt and seen properties, invokes Occam's razor, and asks why an additional material substance is required.

moves.speaker: Matt Dillahunty
moves.proposition: Physical properties and forces describe causal interactions that need not be mentally experienced, and removing those physical components also removes the capacities by which systems interact.
moves.attributionBasis: Matt takes the invited turn and contrasts mental experience with friction, nuclear forces, molecular interaction, and water's physical effects.

components.text: Show that a material substrate adds no necessary explanatory work beyond experienced properties.
Show why the cumulative considerations favor idealism over a physical causal account.

response.rationale: The reply contacts the parsimony premise by assigning physical properties an indispensable causal role and also supplies a physical rival to the idealist inference.

responsivenessWithinClass.rationale: Within full answers, it explicitly contacts the substrate's alleged redundancy, though the defense of physical-property realism remains compressed.

precisionFindings.rationale: The causal-capacity proposition is clear, with only an implicit qualification that physical properties are theoretical descriptions of interactions.

calibrationFindings.rationale: Removing all physical components plausibly removes physical capacities, but the necessity claim assumes rather than fully defends physical-property realism.

charity.alternative: Experienced qualities and informational relations might exhaust what physical-property language describes.
charity.decisiveQualification: Such a view must still explain the observer-independent causal capacities attributed to forces and molecular relations.

logicalCoherence.rationale: The causal-capacity reply coherently rebuts redundancy, although it leaves one bounded implicit bridge from successful physical description to ontology.

evidenceWarrant.rationale: Friction, nuclear forces, and molecular interaction are specific examples, but their mind independence and ontological import are asserted rather than demonstrated.

relevanceBurden.rationale: Within the central tier, this directly advances the con route's indispensable mind-independent causation account.

representationalCharity.rationale: Matt squarely addresses the strongest informational reading by focusing on causal work, with only a minor omission about structuralist alternatives.

moves.evidenceBasis: Matt cites friction, strong and weak nuclear forces, molecular interaction, and water's effects as causal capacities independent of experience.

moves.speaker: Michael Jones
moves.proposition: If idealism is true, the informational distinctions described by physics can refer to qualitatively discernible phenomenal states—including qualia, sensations, thoughts, and mathematics—rather than material arrangements.
moves.attributionBasis: Michael endorses the physical description, then explicitly defines information by contrasting its referent under materialism with its referent under idealism.

components.text: Explain how phenomenal information supplies the causal capacities attributed to physical properties and forces.

response.rationale: Defining information's referent conditionally under idealism clarifies the ontology but does not explain how phenomenal distinctions ground the cited interactions.

responsivenessWithinClass.rationale: Within relevant nonanswers, the conditional account is closely issue-bearing but leaves the decisive causal-grounding demand unanswered.

precisionFindings.rationale: The conditional proposition is explicit, although 'information,' phenomenal states, mathematics, and mental phenomena are grouped too loosely.

calibrationFindings.rationale: The repeated conditional 'if idealism is true' appropriately limits the claim to a possible referent rather than establishing idealism.

logicalCoherence.rationale: The conditional distinction is usable, but it leaves a material bridge between qualitatively discernible states and the full informational structure of physics.

evidenceWarrant.rationale: The appeal to Shannon frames information as distinctions, but the phenomenal referent and inclusion of mathematics remain substantially asserted.

relevanceBurden.rationale: Within the subsidiary tier, it materially supports the affirmative claim that informational description requires no material substrate.

representationalCharity.rationale: The move offers a conditional semantic account and does not materially interpret or characterize a live opposing alternative.

moves.evidenceBasis: Michael conditionally contrasts material arrangements with qualitatively distinguishable phenomenal states as information's referent under idealism.

moves.speaker: Matt Dillahunty
moves.proposition: If physical development is contingent on a mind, evolution and chemical interaction before ordinary observers cannot proceed unless a divine mind is added to sustain or collapse reality.
moves.attributionBasis: Matt explicitly traces the consequences of Michael's view from mind-contingent information to evolution, chemistry, and the introduction of a divine mind.

components.text: Explain how mind-contingent information permits evolution and chemical interaction before ordinary observers.
Show that eliminating material substance preserves a sufficient account of preconscious causal development.

response.rationale: The objection directly tests the mind-contingent ontology against evolution and chemistry and identifies the divine-mind addition apparently needed to preserve development.

responsivenessWithinClass.rationale: Within full answers, it explicitly contacts the decisive physical-development implication of the affirmative ontology.

precisionFindings.rationale: The dilemma is clear, but 'mind' shifts between ordinary observers and a divine mind without fully specifying the relevant dependence.

calibrationFindings.rationale: The challenge is forceful and relevant, but 'can't have evolution at all' assumes the view requires continuous observation rather than informational evolution.

charity.alternative: Unobserved information could evolve lawfully without continuous observation by an ordinary or divine mind.
charity.decisiveQualification: The affirmative must explain how such evolution remains mind-dependent and yields later definite physical history.

logicalCoherence.rationale: The objection exposes a material explanatory demand, though its conditional assumes that mind contingency entails continuous observation or collapse.

evidenceWarrant.rationale: Evolution and chemical interaction are concrete tests, but the inference depends on an incompletely defended reading of the affirmative's observer dependence.

relevanceBurden.rationale: Within the central tier, it directly attacks the affirmative's indispensable account of physical and cosmic development.

representationalCharity.rationale: The objection identifies a serious implication but initially omits the strongest alternative of observer-independent wave-function evolution.

moves.evidenceBasis: Matt argues that mind-contingent information threatens evolution and chemistry before observers and appears to require a divine collapsing mind.

moves.speaker: Michael Jones
moves.proposition: A divine mind need not continuously watch developing events because information in the wave function can evolve deterministically until contact with a conscious observer yields a definite physical appearance through collapse.
moves.attributionBasis: Michael directly answers the challenge, distinguishes deterministic wave-function evolution from observer-induced collapse, and illustrates the distinction with a game analogy.

components.text: Explain how evolution and chemical interaction proceed before ordinary conscious observers without continuous divine observation.

response.rationale: Michael directly answers that informational wave-function evolution proceeds deterministically before observation and reserves collapse for definite appearance to consciousness.

responsivenessWithinClass.rationale: Within full answers, it explicitly contacts the decisive pre-observer development premise and supplies a mechanism-level distinction.

precisionFindings.rationale: The proposed sequence is recoverable, but 'information,' 'physical appearance,' observer, and collapse remain partly underspecified across scales.

calibrationFindings.rationale: The claim presents consciousness-induced collapse and deterministic universal development as settled without acknowledging competing quantum interpretations or technical limits.

charity.alternative: Preconscious evolution requires real interactions and records, not merely a later observer's definite appearance.
charity.decisiveQualification: Deterministic wave-function evolution must account for effective classical records and causal development before observation.

logicalCoherence.rationale: The evolution-collapse distinction answers the immediate dilemma, but leaves a material bridge from an uncollapsed wave function to definite historical development.

evidenceWarrant.rationale: Named authorities and a book support terminology, but the consciousness-collapse interpretation and its cosmological application are substantially asserted.

relevanceBurden.rationale: Within the central tier, this directly supplies the affirmative route's principal account of pre-observer physical development.

representationalCharity.rationale: The answer fairly addresses continuous observation but omits the strongest qualification concerning definite pre-observer records and classical emergence.

moves.evidenceBasis: Michael distinguishes deterministic evolution of wave-function information from consciousness-triggered collapse into a definite physical appearance and invokes Quantum Enigma.

moves.speaker: Matt Dillahunty
moves.proposition: A video-game analogy does not show that unobserved structures cease to exist, because the engine may continue maintaining the simulated environment when the player is absent or looking elsewhere.
moves.attributionBasis: Matt interrogates which observer matters and then uses the continued operation of a game engine to challenge Michael's analogy about off-screen existence.

components.text: Show that the game analogy supports absence of definite unobserved structure rather than merely selective rendering.

response.rationale: Matt directly challenges the analogy by observing that a game engine can continue maintaining simulated structure without the player's attention.

responsivenessWithinClass.rationale: Within full answers, it contacts the analogy's decisive implication, though it does not independently resolve the quantum claim.

precisionFindings.rationale: The limited claim about what the game analogy fails to establish is clear, stable, and properly scoped.

calibrationFindings.rationale: The engine's continued maintenance is offered as a live possibility defeating the analogy, not as proof of physicalism.

charity.alternative: The analogy concerns definite rendering to an avatar, not whether underlying informational state persists.
charity.decisiveQualification: Persistent underlying state does not itself establish definite offscreen spatial structure.

logicalCoherence.rationale: A counterexample involving persistent engine state validly shows that non-rendering does not entail nonexistence or nonmaintenance.

evidenceWarrant.rationale: The familiar engine behavior is a specific and apt counterexample, though no technical detail establishes how all games maintain environments.

relevanceBurden.rationale: Within the subsidiary tier, it directly and strongly tests the limits of the affirmative's video-game analogy.

representationalCharity.rationale: Matt fairly exposes the ambiguity in offscreen existence, with a minor omission about the difference between maintained data and rendered geometry.

moves.evidenceBasis: Matt asks what happens when the player leaves and points out that the game can continue through its engine without another person involved.

moves.speaker: Michael Jones
moves.proposition: Without thinking minds, interaction can persist at an informational level through deterministic wave-function evolution without objects occupying definite positions in a spacetime setting.
moves.attributionBasis: Michael answers Matt's renewed mind-removal question by distinguishing informational interaction from definite spatiotemporal physical existence.

components.text: Clarify what persists and interacts when no thinking observer supplies a definite spatiotemporal presentation.
Account for interaction and development before ordinary conscious observation.

response.rationale: Michael clarifies that informational interaction persists while definite spatiotemporal position does not, directly answering what remains without thinking minds.

responsivenessWithinClass.rationale: Within full answers, it explicitly contacts the persistence question and states the proposed informational-versus-spatiotemporal distinction.

precisionFindings.rationale: The distinction is recoverable, but 'information setting,' interaction, existence, and definite position lack a stable technical account.

calibrationFindings.rationale: The denial of definite spacetime existence is asserted as following from wave-function evolution without addressing decoherence or rival interpretations.

charity.alternative: Unobserved systems may retain definite or effectively definite structure while informational dynamics continue.
charity.decisiveQualification: The absence of need to posit position is not evidence that no definite unobserved structure exists.

logicalCoherence.rationale: Informational interaction is compatible with the proposal, but compatibility does not establish the conclusion that definite spacetime structure is absent.

evidenceWarrant.rationale: The move substantially relies on assertion about the wave function and supplies no discriminating evidence against definite or effectively definite structure.

relevanceBurden.rationale: Within the subsidiary tier, it maximally and directly supplies the affirmative counterfactual account of unobserved interaction.

representationalCharity.rationale: The reply states its own ontology clearly but omits the decisive distinction between explanatory dispensability and evidential absence.

moves.evidenceBasis: Michael says systems interact informationally through deterministic wave-function evolution while lacking definite positions in a spacetime setting.

moves.speaker: Matt Dillahunty
moves.proposition: The claim that physical reality would effectively stop without thinking minds is unfalsifiable and introduces unnecessary complexity under Occam's razor.
moves.attributionBasis: The turn directly follows Michael Jones's explicit confirmation and presents the opposing critique in the live dyadic exchange.

components.text: Provide a discriminating falsification condition for the denial of definite reality without thinking minds.
Justify the additional consciousness-dependent collapse commitment under ontological economy.

response.rationale: The reply directly challenges both testability and parsimony, although it states the objection briefly rather than developing a concrete rival test.

responsivenessWithinClass.rationale: Within full answers, it explicitly contacts the falsifiability and economy implications, with a bounded lack of elaboration.

precisionFindings.rationale: The unfalsifiability and Occam objections are clear, with an implicit restriction to the claimed mind-dependent stoppage.

calibrationFindings.rationale: Matt's repeated uncertainty moderates the claim, though calling it unfalsifiable precedes an exhaustive examination of possible quantum defeaters.

charity.alternative: A consciousness-dependent account could have indirect quantum-mechanical falsifiers even if no observer can witness mindless reality.
charity.decisiveQualification: The proposed falsifier must discriminate consciousness dependence from rival quantum interpretations.

logicalCoherence.rationale: The challenge coherently follows from inaccessible observer-free conditions, but the inference to complete unfalsifiability leaves a material scope condition.

evidenceWarrant.rationale: The inaccessibility concern supports the objection, though no detailed analysis excludes indirect tests or establishes the claimed complexity comparison.

relevanceBurden.rationale: Within the central tier, it directly reaches the con route's indispensable testability and ontological-parsimony bridge.

representationalCharity.rationale: The brief objection identifies the core testability problem but does not consider the strongest possibility of indirect empirical defeat.

moves.evidenceBasis: Matt says he cannot see how to argue against the claim and characterizes it as unfalsifiable and contrary to Occam's razor.

moves.speaker: Michael Jones
moves.proposition: The consciousness-dependent account is claimed to be falsifiable because finding hidden variables compatible with quantum mechanics would undermine its appeal to contextuality and observer-dependent perceived reality.
moves.attributionBasis: The speaker explicitly answers the immediately preceding falsifiability objection and reconnects the answer to his opening quantum-mechanical argument.

components.text: Identify a publicly examinable condition that would falsify the consciousness-dependent account.

response.rationale: Michael directly supplies hidden variables compatible with quantum mechanics as a proposed defeater and links that condition to contextuality and observer dependence.

responsivenessWithinClass.rationale: Within full answers, it explicitly contacts the decisive falsifiability demand with a concrete proposed empirical-theoretical condition.

precisionFindings.rationale: The defeater is recoverable, but hidden variables, contextuality, and consciousness dependence are not distinguished with sufficient technical precision.

calibrationFindings.rationale: The claim that hidden variables must be found overstates what Kochen-Specker excludes and does not qualify contextual hidden-variable possibilities.

charity.alternative: Indirect quantum results may test contextuality without uniquely testing consciousness-dependent collapse.
charity.decisiveQualification: A genuine defeater must discriminate the consciousness ontology from nonconscious contextual interpretations.

logicalCoherence.rationale: The proposed defeater is usable, but the inference substantially conflates noncontextual hidden variables, contextuality, observer dependence, and conscious observation.

evidenceWarrant.rationale: Kochen-Specker and a named experiment provide specific support, yet their asserted bearing on consciousness-dependent reality lacks the necessary interpretive bridge.

relevanceBurden.rationale: Within the central tier, it directly advances the affirmative's indispensable demonstrability bridge by naming a potential defeater.

representationalCharity.rationale: The response offers a concrete condition but materially omits the strongest qualification that contextuality alone does not entail consciousness dependence.

moves.evidenceBasis: Michael invokes experimental confirmation of Kochen-Specker and proposes hidden variables compatible with quantum mechanics as falsifying his observer-dependent account.
